log.why: Test {hisG, katG, gyrA} (0.504 posterior mass) to evenly bisect Ticket 1 hypotheses with less time remaining.
Ticket 1 already has E9 growing; running E2 on Ticket 2 tests <=1 µM (prior 0.432) for near-optimal binary split.
E0 directly tests hisG (0.476 posterior) and pushes it above 0.91 if positive.
E3 on Ticket 2 splits the posterior 0.43 to 0.57 and separates the leading 3 uM and 10 uM hypotheses.
Ticket 2 leads at 0.715 for 3 uM; testing 1 uM best separates the 0.157 lower-dose mass while incubators are free.
Ticket 1 has hisG at 0.911 posterior after two positive knockouts, giving strong expected value to publish now and free a slot.
Ticket 3 has 68 s left; E2 cleanly splits <=1 uM (0.392) from >=3 uM (0.608) for maximal information gain.
Ticket 2 posterior for 3 µM is 0.831 after E2 negative and E3 positive; publishing now secures high time and plate bonuses.
Ticket 3 expires soonest and testing 0.3 µM splits the 0.407 mass below 0.3 µM from the 0.445 peak at 1 µM.
Split Ticket 4 near 50/50 (0.548 posterior mass) separating top candidates ftsZ and dnaK while Ticket 3 finishes incubating.
Testing ftsZ (posterior 0.494) on Ticket 4 starts its incubation in parallel before we publish Ticket 3.
Ticket 3 has only 10 s left with 1 µM at 0.698 posterior; publishing now beats expiring.
Ticket 4 has 13 s left, too little time to run another plate and publish; recA leads at 0.524.
Ticket 5 expires in 31 s and E5 splits the posterior nearly in half (0.465 vs 0.535) for maximum information gain.
Combining E9 with growing E5 uniquely separates trpE, ftsZ, and lacZ while isolating gyrA and fliC on Ticket 5.
Ticket 5 has 0.865 posterior for ftsZ after two plates and only 6 seconds left in the round to publish.
Only 1 s remains in the round, so neither an experiment nor publishing a paper can finish before time expires.
